arguments.text: Plan (min 1): 10 km, 8 legs of 1250 m out-and-back. Start hard (shaft 265 W vs CP 200, boat 169 vs 127). Expect settle by min 2-3. If shaft power still above ~210 W after min 3, cue ease. Current helps on leg 1 (push_along +0.26), so expect opposing on even legs: judge effort by pod shaft power, not GPS pace. Target shaft power near CP (~200 W) mid-race, finish sprint last ~800-1000 m depending on pod reserve.

arguments.message: shaft power still well above CP after the start
pod reserve getting low with a long way to go
shaft power sagging well below CP

text: no cue: start phase, effort expected to settle; set watches for overpacing, low pod reserve, effort sag and the finish.

arguments.text: Settle now, ease to steady race effort, long way

Min 3.5: shaft still 233 W, pod reserve 43 pct, boat reserve 34 pct. Cued ease (no pace target, because current helps this leg ~0.3 m/s and a GPS pace would mislead after the turn). Check at next wake: want shaft near 200-205 W. If still above 215, cue ease again.

text: Cued ease: shaft power 233 W above CP 200 W with pod reserve already at 43 pct and 9.2 km to go.

arguments.text: Ease more, still too hot. Smooth long strokes, save it

Min 4.7: first ease barely took (shaft 233 to 224 W, pod reserve 34 pct). Cued ease again. Leg 2 after turn at ~1250 m is into current (~0.33 m/s), GPS pace will look slow: do not react to GPS pace, watch shaft power. Want 195-205 W.

text: Cued ease again: shaft 224 W still above CP with pod reserve 34 pct and nearly 9 km left.

arguments.text: Into current, ignore the pace. Ease back to steady

arguments.name: drag_gap
arguments.description: local push minus course-fitted push; strongly negative = extra drag (rudder snag) or blade problem

arguments.message: boat slower than shaft power and course current predict: snag on rudder or drag?

arguments.text: Min 7.7: eased to 207 W by min 6, then after turn into current rose back to 220 (chasing GPS pace). Pod reserve 21 pct, boat reserve 1 pct but no fade (-0.4) and paddler says 7/10 hard but holding: hint CP may be underestimated, not proven. Do not change CP yet; wait for cp_implied or fade evidence. Cued ease again. Added drag_gap watch (push_local minus push_along below -0.18) for rudder snag; if it fires and fade shows, consider clear_rudder.

text: Cued ease: shaft 218 W above CP into the current with pod reserve 21 pct; added a drag watch for rudder snags.

arguments.message: still above CP on a low pod reserve: re-cue with a pace target

arguments.text: Min 8.5: paddler ignoring plain ease cues (222 W, pod 14 pct, fade -2.4). Next cue: ease WITH a GPS pace target. Into current (push -0.26): CP 200 W gives water ~3.17, GPS ~2.91 = about 172 s/500. With current (+0.3) next leg: GPS ~3.45 = about 145 s/500. Added hot_recheck watch to wake me when cue gate opens.

text: no cue: cue gate closed for 23 s; set a recheck watch to re-cue ease with a pace target.

arguments.text: Reserve nearly gone. Ease now, let it recover

Min 9.0: pod reserve 11 pct, shaft 219, fade -4.7. GPS speed sliding 3.06 to 2.89 over ~60 s at constant shaft power; drag_gap drifted +0.03 to -0.12 gradually (looks like tiring blade more than a sudden rudder snag, but keep watching). Cued ease with pace 176 s/500 (into current). Next turn ~660 m ahead (about min 12.5): after turn with current, re-cue a pace near 148-150 or plain hold, else 176 is far too slow there.

arguments.condition: (heading_deg < 50 or heading_deg > 310) and elapsed_s > 660 and elapsed_s < 1000
arguments.message: turned onto leg 3 with the current: pace target 176 now too slow, re-cue

text: Cued ease with a 176 s/500 pace target: pod reserve 11 pct at 219 W, speed fading; set a watch to re-cue after the next turn.

arguments.message: cue gate open: send clear_rudder (paddler reported heavy boat, speed down at same shaft power)

arguments.text: Min 9.3: paddler says boat suddenly heavy, something on rudder? Matches data: GPS speed down ~5 pct at constant shaft ~220 W, drag_gap about -0.11. Cost of clear_rudder is a few seconds, gain if snagged is ~0.1 m/s for 8 km (about 2 min). Plan: cue clear_rudder as soon as gate opens (~min 10.2, watch gate_open_clear). Then check drag_gap recovers toward 0; if not, it was fatigue, not weed.

text: no cue: gate closed 49 s; set a watch to send clear_rudder the moment it opens (paddler and data both point to a snag).

arguments.text: Yes, likely weed. One back-stroke to clear the rudder

Min 10.2: sent clear_rudder. Before: drag_gap about -0.17 (push_local -0.44 vs push_along -0.27), speed_water 3.10, shaft 225 W, pod reserve 3.5 pct. The 176 pace target made them push harder because the snag slowed the boat. Next: confirm drag_gap back near 0 and speed up at same shaft; then cue ease (no pace) to get shaft under 200 so the pod reserve refills.

arguments.message: check whether the rudder clear worked (drag_gap, speed) and cue ease if shaft still above CP

text: Cued clear_rudder: paddler reports heavy boat and speed is down 0.17 m/s at the same shaft power; follow-up watch set.

arguments.text: Min 10.9: drag_gap sat at -0.16 then dropped to -0.52 right after the back-stroke (momentum loss, expected transient), now recovering (-0.35). Shaft climbing 222 to 256 W with pod reserve 0: paddler re-accelerating and chasing the old 176 pace. Must cue ease (no pace) at gate open (~min 11.4, after_clear_check watch). Judge snag cleared if drag_gap returns near 0 within ~40 s.

text: no cue: gate closed 25 s; drag dip is the back-stroke transient; will cue ease at gate open via the follow-up watch.

arguments.text: Rudder clear, boat is fast again. Ease right off, recover

Min 11.4: snag cleared: speed_water back to 3.30, fade back to -0.5 (was -7). But shaft 264 W with pod reserve 0 (surging after the back-stroke). Cued ease, no pace. Turn in ~250 m, then leg 3 with current. Want shaft 185-195 W for a few minutes to refill pod reserve. If paddler holds 220+ W on a 0 reserve without fading for 5+ min, CP shaft is probably underestimated: consider set_critical_power.

text: Cued ease: snag cleared and speed recovered, but shaft 264 W on an empty pod reserve.

arguments.text: Current helps now. Ease and let it carry you, settle 2:28

Min 13.2 leg 3 (with current): shaft 240 W, pod reserve 0 for 2+ min, paddler says 8/10 hard but holding. Cued ease with pace 148 s/500 (expect ~200 W shaft if current +0.3). Before the turn drag_gap was still about -0.07: small residual drag or tired blade. Next turn ~min 19 into current: re-cue pace ~172-174 or plain hold. If shaft stays 230+ for 10 min with no fade, CP is underestimated: set cp_shaft ~225.

text: Cued ease with a 148 s/500 target on the leg with the current: shaft 240 W on an empty pod reserve, paddler 8/10.

arguments.message: cue gate open: second clear_rudder (boat still needs ~19 pct more shaft power for the same speed than before the snag)

arguments.name: boat_share
arguments.description: share of pod shaft power reaching the boat (hull model); about 0.63-0.66 before the snag

arguments.text: Min 13.5: KEY: first clear_rudder did not fix it. boat power / shaft power = 0.53 now, same as during the snag (0.54), vs 0.63-0.66 before (min 5-7.6). After the clear, 3.30 m/s needed 264 W vs 218 W before the snag. eta_est has partly absorbed the drag, so drag_gap understates it. Plan: second clear_rudder at gate open (~min 14.3, watch gate_open_clear2). Then check boat_share recovers above 0.6. If it does not, suspect pod drift or tired blade instead.

text: no cue: gate closed; boat still needs about 19 pct more shaft power for the same speed than before the snag, so a second clear_rudder is set for when the gate opens.

arguments.reason: Paddler has done about 27 kJ above the 200 W shaft CP (W prime 18.7 kJ), held 220-250 W for 3+ min on an empty pod and boat reserve with no fade (fade +0.2 now) and reports 8/10 holding. True CP is at least about 8 pct higher; conservative correction.

arguments.message: speed at same rate fading: blow-up, drag or tired blade?
shaft above 240 W for a minute mid-race
shaft power sagging well below the corrected CP (216 W)

arguments.text: Min 14.4: second clear NOT sent: boat_share back to 0.65 (146/224), drag_gap +0.12, fade +0.2, so the snag was cleared by the first back-stroke; the low ratio at min 13.5 was a post-turn artifact. Set CP up to shaft 216 / boat 137 (1 of 3 used): paddler did ~27 kJ above 200 W with no collapse. Paddler self-paces ~220-240 W and mostly ignores ease cues; stop nagging unless fade appears. Watches now: fading, surge (>240 W 60 s), effort_sag (<195 W), drag_jump, finish_plan (1400 m to go).

text: no cue: rudder snag is cleared (boat efficiency back to 0.65), so no second clear; raised CP to 216 W shaft because the paddler has held well above the old CP with no fade.

arguments.name: fade_max_60s
arguments.source:
w = window(fade_pct, 60)
max(w) if len(w) > 0 else 0.0
arguments.description: best fade_pct in the last 60 s: below -3.5 means fade held for a whole minute

arguments.message: speed at same rate down 3.5+ pct for over a minute: blow-up, drag or tired blade?

arguments.text: Min 14.9: fading watch false alarm (5-min minimum still held the snag). Replaced with fade_max_60s (best fade in last 60 s) below -3.5. Current fade -0.1, shaft 226, all fine.

text: no cue: the fade alert was a leftover from the snag (fade now -0.1); fixed the watch to use the last minute only.

arguments.text: Good. This is your race effort, hold it every leg

Min 17.1: paddler says feeling good, steady, at shaft 225-240 W for 6 min, fade +0.9, both reserve models stuck at 0. True shaft CP likely ~230-240 (test underestimated it ~15-20 pct). Cued hold (no pace, current flips each leg). Plan: let them self-pace ~230 W, no more ease cues unless fade below -3.5 for a minute. Finish: start the final sprint ~900-1000 m out since there is probably unused reserve the model cannot see. One CP correction used (216); 2 left.

arguments.message: shaft power sagged below 208 W for a minute (they have been holding 225-240 comfortably)

text: Cued hold: paddler feels good and steady at 230 W with no fade, so this is their sustainable race effort.

arguments.message: drag gap still below -0.15 for 40 s after the turn: real snag, not the turn

arguments.text: Min 19.1: turned onto leg 4 (into current) ~25 s ago; drag_jump fired (gap -0.39) but turns always show a transient (min 13.1 showed -0.43 then cleared). Set drag_persist watch (gap < -0.15 for 40 s) to confirm a real snag before any clear_rudder. Shaft 244 W into current, paddler fine.

text: no cue: drag alert right after a turn is likely the turn transient; set a 40 s persistence watch to confirm before acting.

arguments.text: Boat slowed at the turn. One back-stroke, clear the rudder

Min 19.7: after turn onto leg 4 drag_gap stepped from +0.05 to a steady -0.18 (about 0.23 m/s slower than the pod predicts), fade -5.3. Paddler says 6/10 steady, feels fine (no heavy-boat report, unlike the first snag), so it may instead be a stronger current or new wind on this heading. Cheap test: sent clear_rudder (costs ~4 s). If drag_gap returns near +0.05 within 40 s it was weed; if not, it is current/wind: check leg 5 after the turn at ~5000 m (gap should go positive if current/wind).

arguments.message: check whether the second rudder clear changed drag_gap (weed) or not (current/wind)

text: Cued clear_rudder: boat 0.23 m/s slower than the pod predicts since the turn; cheap test of weed versus stronger current.
no cue: this alert predates the clear_rudder sent 10 s ago; waiting for the post-clear check.

arguments.message: 50 s into leg 5 (with current): read drag_gap; positive means stronger current/wind, negative means residual drag

arguments.text: Min 21.2: after 2nd clear (min 19.9) drag_gap went -0.20 to the back-stroke dip then settled -0.10/-0.11 (partial improvement, still below the +0.05 baseline). push_along creeping -0.28 to -0.37: current may be building over time. No third clear yet. Decide at leg 5 (turn at ~5000 m): gap clearly positive = current/wind, leave it; gap negative = residual drag, clear again. leg5_check watch set. Paddler self-paces 245 W into current, 230 with it: fine.

text: no cue: second clear gave a partial improvement only; will tell weed from stronger current after the next turn.

arguments.text: Min 24.2: SUSPECT POD DRIFT (reading high). Pod shaft crept 245 to 262 W on leg 4 while GPS speed stayed flat 2.81-2.82; paddler says 7/10 feels fine (same as at 220 W at min 7.7); eta_est fell 0.61 to 0.56; boat-model power only 129-131 W (below boat CP 137), boat reserve refilling to 36 pct. Leg 2 vs leg 4 same water: GPS 3.03 at 220 W then, 2.82 at 255 W now. If confirmed, ignore pod numbers (shaft, w_bal_pod, push_local, drag_gap) and pace on boat power, speed_water and feel. Test at leg 5 (with current): if push_along refit stays ~0.37 and drag_gap still negative, it is the pod (or drag); then consider cueing a modest push since paddler has headroom.

text: no cue: pod power rising with flat speed and the paddler at 7/10 points to pod drift; will confirm on the next leg before changing the effort.

arguments.message: on leg 6 into the strengthening current: consider a modest push here

arguments.text: Min 26.9 DIAGNOSIS: current is strengthening over time, push along the axis from leg pairs (N GPS minus S GPS)/2: legs1-2 0.31, legs3-4 0.40, legs4-5 ~0.48; push_along fit lags (0.37-0.38), so leg 4 looked like drag and leg 5 looks fast. Mean water speed per leg pair flat (3.34, 3.22, 3.30) while pod rose 225 to 260+: POD READS HIGH (drift) or blade less efficient; ignore pod numbers. Paddler steady ~140-148 W boat, 7/10, feels fine. Plan: hold; modest push into current on leg 6; finish push from ~1300 m using boat reserve. Removed pod-based watches.

text: no cue: leg 5 shows a normal gap, so leg 4 was a strengthening current, not weed; pod now reads high, so pacing on boat speed and feel; paddler steady.
no cue: steady on leg 5, boat power near CP, fade small; leg 6 watch will prompt a modest push into the current.

arguments.text: Min 32.1 start of leg 6 (into current), 3686 m left. Remaining: leg 6 into (1186 m), leg 7 with (1250 m), leg 8 into current (1250 m) and the finish is on leg 8. Decided NOT to push on leg 6: extra effort is worth the same on leg 8 and spending it there carries no risk of emptying early. Plan: hold legs 6-7; at the last turn (1250 m to go) cue push into the current, then finish cue at ~400 m. finish_plan watch fires at 1400 m.

text: no cue: saving the extra effort for the final leg, which is also into the current; paddler steady.
